solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One not attending to Charles somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive by some unstated route, so they must be rearranged

parts.note: both words taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone is ignoring what is being said to Charles.
explanation.walkthrough: CLOTH-EARS is a British put-down for someone who never listens.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth-ears is a person who fails to hear or heed what is said, so one not paying attention.

clue.text: Volunteers in churches answer an order

indicators.note: the volunteers are placed in the churches, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: CE, Church of England, twice for the plural
the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
A is the usual abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Volunteers in church are given an instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads order as a command, but it is the biological rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Cetacea is the zoological order containing whales, dolphins and porpoises, a classification rank above family.

clue.text: One having sedative after losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a downer is a depressant drug

explanation.surface: Someone takes a sedative once decapitated, an absurd picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is a person who possesses something, the one having it.

clue.text: Respects bad doctor who needs a long time to provide cover

indicators.note: something providing cover wraps around what it shields, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: hours is a colloquial long time
Dr No, the villain of the Bond film

explanation.surface: A hopeless doctor takes ages to arrange cover yet still gets respect.
explanation.walkthrough: Bad doctor is Dr No, the James Bond villain; who needs a long time to provide cover says he is wrapped in the time.
explanation.definitionFit: To honour someone is to respect or esteem them, so honours is a verb synonym of respects.

clue.text: Castellans regularly censored maps

indicators.note: censoring at regular intervals blots out every other letter, keeping the rest

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Castle governors had their maps routinely censored.
explanation.walkthrough: A castellan is the governor of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound collection of maps, so the word stands for maps as a set.

clue.text: WWI battle books discovered in fresh inquest

indicators.note: something discovered in a place is found inside it
a fresh version is newly made, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: A new inquest turns up books about a First World War battle.
explanation.definitionFit: St Quentin in northern France gave its name to battles fought there in the First World War, notably in 1918.

clue.text: Quickly losing recipe for sauce

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away from the word

parts.note: presto is the musical term for fast
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin

explanation.surface: Someone in a hurry has lost the recipe for a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian sauce of basil, pine nuts, garlic and cheese.

clue.text: Dog's stick used for instruction?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gun dog breed
second meaning: a rod a teacher indicates with

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a dog's stick for training; the possessive is just a joining 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer is both a breed of gun dog that indicates game and a teacher's rod for indicating things on a board.

clue.text: Cast to one side?

parts.note: surface reading: thrown aside, discarded
setter's reading: the actors of a play, heading to one side of the boards

explanation.walkthrough: Cast looks like a verb meaning thrown, but it is the noun for a troupe of actors, and the side is a theatre direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage left is a direction telling actors to move to one side of the stage, from their own viewpoint.

clue.text: Where an agent's boss would be stuffed

wordplay.words: Where an agent's boss would be
wordplay.note: a boss sits above, or over, an agent, and a fed is an FBI agent

explanation.surface: An agent's boss, wherever he is, is full of food.
explanation.walkthrough: A fed is American slang for an FBI agent, and the boss is positioned OVER the FED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone overfed has been given too much to eat, so they are stuffed.

clue.text: Sizeable group returned projection

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so read it backwards

parts.note: a nonet is a group of nine, size nine being the joke

explanation.surface: A large party came back with a plan or forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon is the projecting tongue on a piece of wood that fits into a mortise joint.

clue.text: Waste water, for example, having strirred tea

parts.note: water is an example of a liquid

indicators.note: stirred things are mixed about, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written before mixing

explanation.surface: Someone stirring tea is told to pour away the waste water.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue's 'strirred' is a typo for stirred.
explanation.definitionFit: To waste someone is slang for killing them, and liquidate is a euphemism for the same murder.

clue.text: Cautious umpires blessed with triple-century by end of test

indicators.note: blessed is used as a mild curse, suggesting confounded and thus muddled letters

parts.note: taken as written
C is a hundred in Roman numerals, three times

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Careful umpires are rewarded with a triple century at the close of a cricket test match.
explanation.definitionFit: Circumspect means wary and careful about risks, the same as cautious.

clue.text: Insect about to miss a tiny little chap

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so read it backwards
missing a letter means leaving that letter out

parts.note: a flea is a jumping insect

explanation.surface: An insect is about to overlook a tiny fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: An elf is a small mischievous being of folklore, often pictured as a diminutive man.

clue.text: Mr Ben fantasised about setter, perhaps some might say

indicators.note: brought about means turned round and rearranged

parts.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Mr Benn, the children's cartoon character, daydreams about the setter.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Benn is a British children's cartoon character who has fantasy adventures; setter also means the compiler, but here it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog is popularly called man's best friend, and a setter is one kind of dog, hence perhaps.

clue.text: Semi-dismissed before church finds something underfoot?

indicators.note: semi means half, so only half the word is kept

parts.note: axed means sacked
a minster is a large church

explanation.surface: Someone partly fired ahead of going to church finds something on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: Positional 'before' in a down clue puts the first part above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: An Axminster is a type of woven carpet named after the Devon town, and carpets lie beneath our feet.

clue.text: Immoderate view merits broadcast under former leader of men

parts.note: ex is a prefix for former

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An extreme opinion gets airtime under a former party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, under means placed below, so EX comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Extremism is the holding of radical political opinions, an outlook lacking moderation.

clue.text: Summing up after a long court battle

definitions.text: Summing up after a long court battle

parts.note: surface reading: a protracted legal case
setter's reading: a tennis court, where the umpire announces the winner

explanation.walkthrough: Court suggests law and summing up a judge's address; on a tennis court the umpire's final call ends the match.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the tennis umpire's call at the end of a match, and figuratively means complete victory.

clue.text: Approach turn at sea

definitions.meaning: second meaning: change tack in a sailing boat

explanation.definitionFit: To go about a job is to set about tackling it; sailors go about when they tack through the wind.

clue.text: Certainly negative and very cold

definitions.meaning: first meaning: below nought, so definitely a minus number

explanation.walkthrough: Certainly negative sounds like a firm refusal, but it is about numbers below nought.
explanation.definitionFit: A sub-zero figure is below nought and so must be a minus number; sub-zero weather is freezing.

clue.text: Kind of swallow one drink

parts.note: the martin is a bird of the swallow family
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One gulp of a single drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Swallow looks like a verb for drinking, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth.

clue.text: Economically use repaired bus under control?

indicators.note: what is under control is in hand, so the next piece is held inside

parts.note: to have a hand in something is to control it

indicators.note: something repaired has been put back together, here in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A frugal operator keeps a mended bus in check.
explanation.walkthrough: Under control means in hand, so the shuffled letters go inside HAND: H-USB-AND.
explanation.definitionFit: To husband resources is to manage them thriftily, a verb meaning to use economically.

clue.text: Sacha Baron Cohen finally gets her

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of each preceding word

parts.note: the last letter of each of the three names

explanation.surface: The comedian Sacha Baron Cohen at last wins a woman over.
explanation.definitionFit: Ann is a female given name, so she can be referred to by the pronoun as a woman.

clue.text: Geek almost filling in gun permit somewhere in the Alps

indicators.note: a filling goes in between, so it sits inside the other pieces
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the Bren is a British light machine gun
a nerd is a geek
a pass allows entry

explanation.surface: A geek almost manages to get a gun licence while in the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brenner Pass is a mountain pass through the Alps between Austria and Italy.

clue.text: With more of these, you'll want more

definitions.text: With more of these, you'll want more

parts.words: With more of these, you'll want more
parts.note: surface reading: something addictive that leaves you craving
setter's reading: requirements, since each extra one is another thing lacking

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a description of an addictive treat, but the more requirements you have, the more you lack.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs are things required or lacking, so having more of them means wanting more.

clue.text: British going after ex boxer, one making a plea?

parts.note: Muhammad Ali, the former heavyweight champion
B is the abbreviation for British
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Briton chases a retired boxer, who offers an excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: Going after puts B after ALI.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a defence plea that the accused was elsewhere when the crime occurred.

clue.text: Secret lover bit this without authority

indicators.note: the phrase says the lover is the word bit plus this answer, so what remains after bit goes is wanted

parts.note: a bit on the side is a clandestine lover

explanation.surface: A secret lover nibbled this without permission.
explanation.walkthrough: A bit on the side is British slang for an illicit lover; drop the bit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done on the side is done unofficially or secretly, outside proper sanction.

clue.text: Brief affairs occupying one chief of antipodean island

indicators.note: occupiers move in, so this piece sits inside the others

parts.note: Roman numeral one
the first letter
biz is short for business

explanation.surface: Holiday flings involving an Australian boss on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is a Spanish island in the Balearics, famous for clubbing holidays.

clue.text: Trunk's approximately on time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
or so means roughly

explanation.surface: A trunk arrives roughly when expected.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, on means placed after, so ORSO follows T.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, without head or limbs.

clue.text: Hoaxed or stymied if confused

indicators.note: confused things are mixed up, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: both words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Tricked, or simply baffled and confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hoaxed has been bamboozled or fooled, and mystified also means bewildered by a deception.
